correctness.rationale: For each of 329 anonymous approval profiles with 1 to 4 voters and three projects, the supplied executable constructs an exact globally maximizing Nash allocation using first-order KKT certificates. Concavity proves global optimality. Uniqueness of the reported utility vector identifies the entire optimum face; the checker enumerates all vertices and all unilateral nonempty-ballot deviations with exact rational or sqrt(17) arithmetic. Results are 0,0,0,6 manipulable profiles and 12 profitable reports at n=4 in two project-symmetry orbits, with exact gains 5/4 and (9-sqrt(17))/4. The two-project all-electorates immunity is independently proved by the Nash singleton-support formula. Finite exhaustion is confined to the stated finite domain.

evidence: Aziz–Lederer–Vollen (2026), Theorem 3: unrestricted Nash incentive ratio is 2; Theorem 4 establishes optimality under broad fairness/efficiency axioms. Its displayed families vary the candidate or voter counts and do not certify the sharp four-voter three-project maximum 5/4.
Aziz–Bogomolnaia–Moulin (2017) provide large-scale excludable manipulation examples; Brandl et al. (2020) address different contribution-funded projects.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A universal upper bound of two is logically weaker than an exact 5/4 ceiling in one fixed finite cell. General failure of strategyproofness does not identify the smallest cell, six exceptional anonymous profiles, two orbits, all tie resolutions or the two exact gains.

value.rationale: The recent general incentive-ratio-two theorem leaves open how early actual manipulation appears in small, commonly implementable participatory-budget elections and how sharp the incentive is at first failure. The present complete first-layer census distinguishes two exact structural ballot families, shows tie-independence, and sharpens the worst-case gain to 5/4 for four voters and three projects. The universal two-project strategyproof boundary is directly relevant to mechanism choice. These are natural size and incentive invariants, not an arbitrary parameter slice; neither the known asymptotic bound nor a single witness gives their values.
